questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
questions.problem:
$$
C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -7 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $C$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =2$ is an eigenvalue of $C$
- $\lambda =5$ is an eigenvalue of $C$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =5$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,C-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
C-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & -7 & 6 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(C-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $4$th column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & -7 & 6 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & 0 \\ -5 & 2 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5-\lambda )\cdot (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 4 \\ -5 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )^{2}\cdot ((2-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )+20) & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)^{2}({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +14) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $D<0$ for the polynomial ${\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +14$ we have that the only real eigenvalue is $\lambda =5$ (with algebraic multiplicity $2$). 

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues of a General 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5 & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,C-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
C-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(C-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -12 \\ 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-6)|\begin{aligned}4 & 5-\lambda  \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1)-3(-4\lambda +8)-6(-3+3\lambda ) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}+7\lambda +4)-(-12\lambda +24)-(-18+18\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda +2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
questions.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -14\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =0$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- $\lambda =-14$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -3 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & -\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -14-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -3 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & -\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -14-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & -2-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & -14-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2-\lambda )\cdot (-14-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0 \\ 3 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-14-\lambda )(-\lambda )(-2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda +14)\lambda (\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda =2,$ $\lambda =-2,$ $\lambda =0,$ and $\lambda =-14$  (all with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
questions.problem:
$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $D$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =2$ is an eigenvalue of $D$
- $\lambda =-1$ is an eigenvalue of $D$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =-1$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,D-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
D-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda  & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -\lambda  & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(D-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(D-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda  & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -\lambda  & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(-\lambda )-2) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +7)({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +7)(\lambda -2)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2}(\lambda +7)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $D$ are $\lambda =-1$ (with algebraic multiplicity $2$), $\lambda =-7$ and $\lambda =2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

questions.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$R=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,R-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
R-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(R-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st column, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(R-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -\lambda  & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 4 \\ 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda -4)+2(-2\lambda +7) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -4)+(-4\lambda +14) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda -10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
